newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil seen flat to 50 cts down, Brent steady.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil seen flat to 50 cts down, Brent steady.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures were called to open unchanged to 50 cents lower on Tuesday while Brent was expected to open fairly steady after last trading on Monday at a yearly spot low.
July Brent last traded at $17.54, before settling at $17.56 a barrel. The last time the front month contract dipped below $17.54 was last June, when it hit $17.48.
June gas oil closed $4.25 a tonne lower on Monday at $160.00.
The July Brent contract was at $17.53/$17.60 a barrel on SIMEX.
"The crude is due to come in unchanged, maybe five cents either way, but we're seeing a little buying interest in Singapore in the last half hour," said one broker.
Key support was seen in the $17.50/$17.54 region.
"It's not strong support but key support in that area...that's the big test today to see if we can hold above it," said one broker.

Brokers said that while there was buying interest in the market, traders were likely to hold out until after the release of weekly U.S. stocks data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) due after the close of trade on Tuesday.
"A lot of people want to buy but they'll be afraid to do it today. They'll wait to see what the APIs look like," said one dealer.
Traders are waiting for a fresh indication of U.S. gasoline, which has so far failed to live up to expectations since the driving season got underway in May.
Last week's report showed record refinery runs and rising crude oil inventories, which helped hack $1.20 a barrel off the value of Brent and $2.20 off NYMEX crude.
